description: Text for escort a short haul.

title: Escort to {destination}
Close escort: {tonnes} t of {cargo}
Guard duty for {faction}
Minder wanted, {destination} run
task: {client} has {tonnes} t of {cargo} bound for {destination} and a hauler crew that won't fly it unescorted.
A single freighter with {tonnes} t of {cargo} needs a gun beside it from {system} to {destination}.
{faction} wants an escort for a {cargo} run to {destination}. Keep the hauler alive and in formation.
Fly cover for {client}'s {cargo} shipment as far as {destination}.
detail: The hauler is slow and the crew nervous. Stay within a kilometre of it.
It has no weapons worth the name, so you are the whole defence.
Arrive within {deadline}.
Raiders have been seen on this lane, though nothing is confirmed.
success: The hauler docks at {destination} without a scratch. {faction} pays {reward} and the hauler crew buy the first round.
{tonnes} t of {cargo} arrive intact. {faction} pays {reward} and asks for you by name next time.
You see the hauler to its berth and the crew shake your hand. {reward} lands in your account within the hour.
Nobody fired a shot at you. {faction} pays {reward} anyway, which is the point of an escort.
failure: The hauler never made it to {destination}. {faction} wants to know where you were.
You lost the hauler on the way. {faction} will not be paying, and says so loudly.
The {cargo} went down with the freighter. {faction} blames your escort, and the crew who got out agree.
The hauler turned back at the first sign of trouble and so, it seems, did you. No pay.

title: Ore train to {destination}
Escort the {cargo} haulers
Raiders on the ore lane
Gun cover for {faction}'s haulers
task: {faction} sends {tonnes} t of {cargo} to {destination} and has lost haulers on this lane before. They want you flying top cover.
Raiders are working the lane out of {system}. Take the ore haulers through to {destination}.
A string of ore haulers leaves {system} for {destination}. You are the escort, and the only one they could afford.
Escort {client}'s haulers and their {cargo} to {destination}, and shoot anything that closes uninvited.
detail: Two haulers went missing last week. Nobody found wreckage, which suggests somebody found the cargo.
The raiders like to hit the rear hauler first.
The convoy will not wait for you, so be at the dock within {deadline}.
If you see where the raiders come from, someone will pay to know.
success: The haulers dock at {destination} one after another, all of them. {faction} pays {reward}. One of the pilots mentions a signal she did not like on the way, and you make a note of it.
The raiders showed up, took one look at you and left. {faction} pays {reward}.
You bring the whole convoy in. {faction} pays {reward} and the haulers' crews buy you drinks you do not need.
{tonnes} t of {cargo} is safe at {destination}. {faction} pays {reward}. You have a fair idea which way the raiders ran.
failure: A hauler was lost, and {faction} does not count the rest as a success. No pay.
The raiders took the lot. {faction} says an escort should have been harder to get past.
You were out of position when it started. The convoy scattered and {faction} has stopped answering your messages.
The {cargo} never reached {destination}. The raiders are richer and you are not.

title: Lane sweep in {system}
Patrol: {system}
Show the flag in {system}
Sweep and report
task: {faction} wants the lanes around {system} swept and the traffic reassured.
Fly a patrol through {system} and deal with anything that shouldn't be there.
The lanes in {system} have gone untended. Patrol them for {deadline} and report what you find.
{client} needs eyes and guns in {system} to keep the freight moving.
detail: Check the beacons and the debris fields in particular.
Hostile contacts are yours to engage. Anything else, log it and move on.
Traders have been reporting odd transponder pings out past the beacons.
Nothing is known to be out there. That is what worries {client}.
success: Your sweep of {system} is logged and closed. {faction} pays {reward}.
You flushed out two chancers and left the rest alone. {faction} pays {reward}.
The lanes are quiet and the traders know why. {faction} pays {reward}.
You found nothing worth shooting and plenty worth noting. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: You never finished the sweep of {system}. {faction} sends someone else.
Something got past you in {system} and {faction} has the losses to prove it.
The patrol log is thin and {faction} does not believe it. No pay.
You left {system} early and the traders noticed.

title: Gate watch at {system}
Hold the gate in {system}
Inspection cover
Warden support in {system}
task: The gate at {system} is under tighter watch and {faction} needs another ship on station.
{client} is running inspections at {system} and wants armed cover for the wardens.
Hold position by the gate in {system} and back the inspectors if anyone makes a run for it.
Patrol the approach to the gate at {system}. Stop and identify anything that will not identify itself.
detail: Passengers are being turned back and tempers are short.
Some of the traffic will try to bolt rather than be searched.
Expect {deadline} of dull work punctuated by one bad minute.
You will be asked to look at things that are none of your business. Do it anyway.
success: The gate held and nobody was hurt. {faction} pays {reward}.
You turned back three runners and a great deal of bad feeling. {faction} pays {reward}.
The wardens thank you in the tone of people who would rather not need to. {faction} pays {reward}.
The inspections finish on time. {faction} pays {reward}, and the queue is somebody else's problem now.
failure: A ship ran the gate while you watched. {faction} wants to know why you did not stop it.
You stood aside at the wrong moment, and the inspectors will say so in their report.
The watch broke down in {system}. {faction} will not be calling again.
You fired on a ship that had every right to be there. {faction} is not paying and will be apologising for you.

title: Bounty: {target}
Wanted: {target}
Bring in {target}
{target}, dead or alive
task: {target} has been jumping contracts around {system} and {client} wants it ended.
There is a price on {target}, last seen in {system}. {faction} will pay for proof.
{faction} wants {target} found and brought to heel. How you do it is your affair.
Find {target}. {client} has had enough of the losses and has put money behind that feeling.
detail: Last known to be flying a stripped courier.
The target is not a soldier, but will fight if cornered.
The price stands for {deadline}.
The paperwork says alive. The client's tone says otherwise.
success: You hand over {target}, or what is left of them, and {faction} pays {reward}. The client seems oddly interested in what {target} was carrying.
{target} is not going to trouble {system} again. {faction} pays {reward}.
The bounty clears. {faction} pays {reward} and does not ask how.
{target} came quietly in the end. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: {target} slipped away and {faction} withdraws the offer.
You lost {target} in the debris. Someone else will collect.
Another hunter reached {target} first. {faction} pays them and not you.
{target} was never where the tip said. {faction} blames you anyway.

title: Registry bounty: {target}
Find {target}
Unregistered: {target}
Sweep target: {target}
task: The registry sweep has turned up {target}, a synth who never registered, and {faction} wants them located in {system}.
{client} has named {target} as an unregistered synth hiding near {system}. Find them and bring them in.
{faction} is paying to close the registry sweep in {system}. {target} is the last name on the list.
Track {target} down and deliver them to {faction}'s officers.
detail: Opinion on the sweep is divided, and {client} knows it.
The target has friends who will not take kindly to being asked questions.
There is a price for the job and a price for not asking why.
The warrant is valid. Whether it is just is not part of the contract.
success: You deliver {target} and {faction} pays {reward}. Nobody meets your eye on the way out.
The sweep closes on {target}. {faction} pays {reward}.
{target} is in custody. {faction} pays {reward}, and the dock goes quiet as you pass.
You hand over the warrant's subject. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: {target} was warned and gone before you arrived. {faction} is displeased.
You lost the trail in {system}. The warrant stays open and the price drops.
Someone beat you to {target}. You did not see who. {faction} pays nothing.
The contract lapsed with {target} still at large.

description: Text for run the blockade: medicine.

title: Blockade run to {destination}
Slip the cordon: {destination}
Medicine past the picket
{tonnes} t of {cargo}, no questions
task: {destination} is cut off by a blockade, and {client} needs {tonnes} t of {cargo} to get through it.
Get {tonnes} t of {cargo} past the picket and into {destination}. The patrols will not be pleased.
{faction} wants the blockade of {destination} run, quietly and in one piece.
Carry {cargo} through the cordon to {destination}. Nobody is going to give you permission.
detail: The pickets fire without hailing.
There is a gap in the patrol schedule, if the information is good.
The deadline is {deadline}, and people at {destination} are counting.
Run dark and keep your drive cold until the last moment.
success: You slip through the cordon and into {destination}. {faction} pays {reward}. The {cargo} is carried off before the picket has finished arguing about you.
The pickets never saw you. {faction} pays {reward}.
{tonnes} t of {cargo} reach {destination}. {faction} pays {reward} and, for once, thanks you too.
You burn the last of your fuel getting in, but you get in. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The picket caught you short of {destination}. The {cargo} is impounded.
You turned back before the cordon. {faction} understands, and still does not pay.
The cordon was tighter than the tip said. You lost the cargo and {faction} lost patience.
The cargo never reached {destination}, and neither did the people who needed it.

title: Convoy escort to {destination}
Escort screen: {tonnes} t of {cargo}
Run the convoy through {system}
Raiders on the convoy road
task: {faction} is gathering a convoy at {system} for {destination}, with {tonnes} t of {cargo} among it. You are one of the escorts.
Join the convoy to {destination} as one of its guns. The raiders have been picking off ships that travel alone, and now they will meet a crowd.
Take station beside the convoy leaving {system} for {destination}. You will have two other escorts, and the raiders will probably have more ships than that.
{client} needs the convoy to {destination} protected. You cannot cover all of it, so cover your assigned ships.
detail: Expect a fight at the gate, where they like to wait.
Your assigned haulers carry the {cargo}.
Keep your wingmates in sight and your haulers closer.
The convoy leaves in {deadline}, with or without you.
success: The raiders hit the convoy at the gate. You held your part of the line and the haulers got through. {faction} pays {reward}.
One hauler was lost further back, but yours made it to {destination}. {faction} pays {reward}.
The convoy docks at {destination}. {faction} pays {reward} and the other escorts salute you at the bar.
The raiders broke before the convoy did. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The convoy scattered at the gate and you could not hold your haulers together. {faction} counts the losses against you.
Your hauler died in the first volley. The rest of the convoy made it, and {faction} will remember which one did not.
The raiders cut through the screen. {faction} blames the escorts, and you are an escort.
You reached {destination} with an empty formation and nothing to show for it.

description: Text for raid a supply depot.

title: Depot raid in {system}
Burn the stores at {system}
Hit and withdraw: {system}
Strike on a forward depot
task: {faction} wants the enemy's forward depot at {system} struck. You are one of the ships it can spare.
A small force is hitting a supply depot in {system}. Your job is the defence suppression, so the bombers can do theirs.
Raid the depot at {system}. {client} wants fuel tanks burning and nothing else touched.
Join a raiding party against a depot in {system}, and be gone before the response arrives.
detail: The garrison is small and will call for help. Expect it within minutes.
Your orders are to leave nothing to be used and nothing to be proved.
The window is {deadline}. After that the depot rotates its guard.
This will not win the war. It will make the next month of it harder for the other side.
success: The depot burns and your party withdraws without losing a ship. {faction} pays {reward}. It is one raid in a long war, but a good one.
You suppressed the guns and the bombers did the rest. {faction} pays {reward}.
The stores at {system} are ash. {faction} pays {reward} and will find another depot for you.
You got out before the garrison's reinforcements arrived. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The depot was reinforced the night before. Your party pulled out with losses and {faction} is not pleased.
The raid failed in {system} and the depot stands. {faction} pays only the dead.
You were pinned by the garrison's guns while the bombers turned back. {faction} will not be paying.
Somebody warned the garrison. {faction} suspects you or your client list.

description: Text for raid a pirate haven.

title: Pirate haven: {system}
Smoke the nest in {system}
Raid in {system}
Clear out {system}
task: Raiders have a hideout in {system}, and {faction} wants it burned out. You are one of several ships it has hired.
A pirate haven in {system} has become too comfortable. Hit it hard with the others.
{client} has located the raiders' anchorage in {system} and will pay for every ship that helps clear it.
Join the strike on the haven at {system} and keep the pirates from scattering.
detail: There are more of them than you are used to.
Whoever pays them also supplies them. If you find the ledger, bring it.
Strike inside {deadline}, before the pirates move on.
Anything with a transponder that will not answer is fair game.
success: The haven is smoke and drifting hull plates. {faction} pays {reward}. Among the wreckage you pick up a ledger, with a name in it.
The pirates scattered, and most of them did not get far. {faction} pays {reward}.
You held the near side of the anchorage while the others went in. {faction} pays {reward}.
The strike was messy and it worked. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The pirates were waiting. The strike broke up and so did the contract.
Half the force never arrived and the haven held. {faction} withdraws payment.
You were driven off with the rest. {faction} does not pay for a failed raid.
The haven was empty when you got there, and the raiders were elsewhere, doing worse.

title: Border picket: {system}
Hold the line at {system}
Contested space: {system}
Picket duty in {system}
task: {faction} is posting pickets along a disputed border at {system}. You are one ship of a thin line.
Patrol the contested space at {system} and challenge anything that crosses without leave.
Join the picket line in {system}, and be ready to stand when the other side tests it.
Hold your sector of the line at {system} for {deadline}.
detail: Your orders are to challenge, not to start a war.
The other side is doing the same on its side. Nobody wants the first shot.
You have a stretch of nine kilometres and two wingmates.
Report any sign of a build-up. The brass wants numbers.
success: Your sector held and nobody crossed it. {faction} pays {reward}. Your sighting reports are read with interest.
The other side tested the line and you stopped them. {faction} pays {reward}.
You rotate out with a clean log. {faction} pays {reward}.
You saw what the picket was meant to see. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The picket was outflanked, and your sector gave first. {faction} does not pay for gaps.
You let a patrol cross and {faction}'s report reads badly for you.
You missed the build-up. {faction} has a different view of its border now.
The line broke and the contract with it.

description: Text for run the blockade: fuel.

title: Fuel for {destination}
Past the picket: {tonnes} t of {cargo}
Blockade run, {destination}
Dark run to {destination}
task: {destination} is running low on {cargo} and the blockade is closing. {faction} needs {tonnes} t delivered through it.
Carry {tonnes} t of {cargo} past the warships to {destination}. You are one of several runners tonight.
{client} has put together a run of ships to break the supply cordon around {destination}. You carry {cargo}.
Run {tonnes} t of {cargo} through the blockade. The guns will see you if the timing is wrong.
detail: The pickets rotate on a schedule. You will be given it, and then told it is probably wrong.
Not every runner will get through, and the plan allows for that.
You have {deadline}, and the cordon tightens every day.
You will fly dark, with the drive on its lowest burn.
success: You are one of three runners to reach {destination}, and your {cargo} is among what arrives. {faction} pays {reward}.
The pickets fired on you and missed. {faction} pays {reward}.
{tonnes} t of {cargo} is on the dock at {destination}. {faction} pays {reward}.
You came through with the tanks nearly dry. {faction} pays {reward} and a bonus in thanks.
failure: Your run did not make it. The {cargo} was lost with the ship that carried it, or close enough.
The pickets were waiting and you turned back. {faction} wants another run, from someone else.
You were caught short of {destination}. The cargo is impounded and so, briefly, are you.
Two of the runners got through. You were not one of them.

title: Bounty: {target}, turncoat captain
Bring down {target}
The {target} contract
Mercenary bounty: {target}
task: {target} led a company of hired guns into the uprising, and {faction} wants them stopped.
The mercenary uprising has a face, and it is {target}. {client} will pay to see it removed from {system}.
{target} turned their company on their own employer. Find them in {system}.
Hunt {target}, now commanding a stolen gunship near {system}.
detail: Their crew is loyal and well armed.
The captain will not be alone. Expect an escort of three or four.
Other hunters are on this bounty. You will not be the only one.
The bounty stands for {deadline}.
success: {target} went down fighting and their company scattered. {faction} pays {reward}. In their strongbox you find a contract with a different client's seal on it.
The uprising lost its leader. {faction} pays {reward}.
You broke {target}'s company at {system}. {faction} pays {reward}.
{target} is dead and the guns are quiet. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: {target} was better guarded than the briefing said. You were driven off and {faction} has other hunters.
The captain escaped to the outer system. {faction} withdraws the bounty.
Your gunship took too much damage to continue. {faction} does not pay for retreats.
A rival hunter claimed {target}. {faction} pays them, not you.

description: Text for assault on the raider base.

title: Raider base in {system}
Assault the hidden base
Strike at {system}
The trail ends in {system}
briefing: #voice:opener# Your last job turned up a trail, and it leads to {system}. #detail# #voice:payment#
#voice:opener# The signals you logged point to a base in {system}. #detail# #voice:urgency# #voice:payment#
task: {faction} has found the raiders' base at {system} and wants it destroyed.
A hidden raider base sits in {system}, and {client} will pay to see it gone.
Strike the raiders' base in {system} with the force {faction} has assembled.
detail: The base is small but heavily armed.
You will fly with others, but the raiders have the advantage of ground they know.
There may be prisoners. Do not shoot the transports.
Whoever sold the raiders their guns will not like what you find.
success: The base is gone and the raiders with it. {faction} pays {reward}. The people who armed them are still out there, and so is the work of finding them.
You broke the base with the rest of the strike force. {faction} pays {reward}.
The raiders' anchorage at {system} is wreckage. {faction} pays {reward}.
{faction} pays {reward} and puts your name on the clear-out list.
failure: The base held and the strike force withdrew. {faction} is not paying for that.
You lost your wingmates in the approach and {faction} blames the intelligence, and you.
The raiders were warned and gone before you arrived, leaving a trap in their place.
The assault failed at {system}. The raiders are still there and so, less happily, are you.

title: Bounty: {target}, the paymaster
Who paid for it: {target}
Settle with {target}
The man behind it: {target}
briefing: #voice:opener# The trail from your last job leads to {target}. #detail# #voice:payment#
task: {target} paid for the trouble, and {faction} wants them found in {system}.
The ledger you recovered names {target}. {client} is willing to put a price on them.
{target} has been funding raiders and hired guns from behind a shop front in {system}. Find them.
detail: They will have protection, probably the paid kind.
Do not expect an honest answer from anybody who knows them.
The bounty stands for {deadline}.
They are patient, and have been waiting for this.
success: {target} is taken, and with them the thread that held the whole thing together. {faction} pays {reward}.
You found {target} in {system}. {faction} pays {reward}.
The paymaster is in custody. {faction} pays {reward} and the rest of the ring scatters.
{target} had more friends than expected and fewer than needed. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: {target} was gone before you reached {system}. The ring will be back.
The paymaster had your measure and your route. {faction} withdraws the bounty.
You were led to the wrong dock. {target} is richer and you are not.
Someone else collected {target}, and for a different client.

title: Screen the carrier at {system}
Carrier screen: {system}
Picket for the flagship
Escort wing, fleet action
task: {faction} is bringing a carrier into {system}, and every light hull in range is screening it. You are one of forty.
A fleet action is coming to {system}. Your wing's job is to keep the carrier's flank clear of fighters and torpedoes.
Take station on the carrier at {system}. You will not see the whole battle. Nobody will.
Screen {client}'s carrier during the action at {system}, and shoot whatever tries to reach it.
detail: Your orders will come over the squadron net, and you will follow them.
Commissioned officers only. The brass wants hands it can trust.
Expect the first wave in minutes and the second in ten.
The carrier will not wait for you to turn round. Neither will the fleet.
success: The carrier launched her last wing and withdrew whole. {faction} pays {reward}. Whether the day was won is for the admirals, but your screen held.
You held your flank through three waves. {faction} pays {reward}. The fleet took the field, and you helped.
The carrier is safe. {faction} pays {reward} and your wing gets a mention in dispatches.
The carrier stayed afloat and so did you. {faction} pays {reward}. The battle itself is still being counted.
failure: The carrier was hit despite your screen, and {faction} blames the escort wing as a whole. You are part of that whole.
You held your line. The fleet didn't. {faction} pays nothing for a lost carrier, whatever the screen did.
The screen broke in the second wave. {faction} will remember who was on that flank.
The carrier survived by turning for home and you were left covering a retreat. No pay.

title: Fleet picket at {system}
Forward screen, {system}
Early warning in {system}
Eyes for the fleet
task: {faction}'s fleet is massing near {system}, and you are one of the pickets out ahead of it.
Fly forward picket for the fleet at {system} and report any sign of the enemy.
{client} wants early warning in {system}. You are one of a dozen small ships posted around the fleet.
Hold a picket station in {system} while the fleet prepares.
detail: You are to run, not to fight, if the enemy comes in force. The fleet needs the warning more than it needs another dead picket.
Keep your transponder quiet and your reports short.
You will not see the fleet's battle, only its beginning.
The station is {deadline} of watching empty space.
success: Your warning reached the fleet with minutes to spare. {faction} pays {reward}. What the admiral did with those minutes is for the admiral.
You called the enemy's approach and fell back in good order. {faction} pays {reward}.
The picket did its job. {faction} pays {reward}. The fleet is where it needs to be.
Your station held until the fleet came up behind you. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The picket was overrun before your warning went out. {faction} lost the minutes it counted on.
You called it late. The fleet formed under fire and {faction} notes your report.
You held the station, and the fleet never listened. {faction} pays you, but it was not enough to save the day.
You abandoned the picket too early. {faction} will not be paying.

title: Strike wing over {system}
Run the strike on {system}
Fleet strike: {system}
Alpha wing, {system}
task: {faction} is hitting the enemy fleet at {system}, and you are flying with a strike wing of sixty ships.
A fleet action has opened at {system}. Your wing is to go in with the first rush and take out the enemy's gun line.
{client} is committing every light hull to the strike on {system}. Your wing is one of six.
Fly with the strike wing against the enemy's fleet at {system}.
detail: You will take orders from the wing commander. Question them afterwards.
Your target is a screening destroyer. You will not see the capital ships.
The first pass is the dangerous one.
Commissioned officers only. The risks are what they are.
success: You were one of sixty ships over {system}. Your target went down, and {faction} pays {reward}. The enemy fleet broke, and you did a little of the breaking.
Your wing took out its destroyer and came home with all but two. {faction} pays {reward}.
The gun line collapsed. {faction} pays {reward}, and the fleet moves in behind you.
You put your shots where they were needed. {faction} pays {reward}.
failure: The strike failed at {system}. You fought well, but the enemy's fleet was stronger than the briefing.
You held the wing's flank and the wing broke around you. {faction} pays for results.
The destroyer you were sent after was a decoy, and the real gun line shredded the wing.
You got out, and many did not. {faction} will not be paying.

title: Break the blockade at {destination}
Convoy under fire: {destination}
Fleet-supported run
Breaking the cordon
task: {faction} is breaking the blockade of {destination} with force, and your ship carries {tonnes} t of {cargo} in the first wave.
A relief fleet is forcing the cordon around {destination}. You are one of the supply ships under its guns.
{client} has raised a relief fleet to run the blockade of {destination}. You are a small part of that fleet, and the cargo is not small.
Fly in with the relief fleet, drop your {cargo} at {destination} and get out.
detail: The warships will do the fighting. You are to get through the gap they make.
You will be one of dozens, and the gap will not stay open long.
The gap opens at a time given on the fleet net. Be ready.
Some ships will not come out. The plan accepts that.
success: The fleet forced the cordon and you flew through the gap with {tonnes} t of {cargo}. {faction} pays {reward}. The blockade is not broken for good, but {destination} will eat this month.
Your {cargo} reached {destination} under the fleet's guns. {faction} pays {reward}.
You were one of the ships that mattered. {faction} pays {reward}.
The gap held long enough. {faction} pays {reward} and the fleet pulls back behind you.
failure: The fleet could not hold the gap and the supply ships turned back. You carried the {cargo} home, and {faction} pays nothing for that.
The cordon closed and you were caught on the wrong side of it. The cargo was lost.
You made it through. The fleet didn't, and {destination} is still under blockade. {faction} pays only for the effort.
The relief failed at {destination}. You fought well, but the cordon was stronger.

description: Text for suppress the mercenary fleet.

title: Mercenary suppression, {system}
Put down the uprising
Strike wing: {system}
The turncoat fleet at {system}
task: The mercenary companies at {system} have turned on their employers, and {faction} is sending the fleet to put them down. You are one wing of it.
A mercenary fleet holds {system}. {client} wants it cleared, and you are one of a hundred ships that will clear it.
Join the assault on the rebel mercenaries at {system}. Your wing is assigned to their picket line.
The uprising makes its stand at {system}. Fly with {faction}'s fleet and break it.
detail: Some of the rebels used to fly beside you.
They know the fleet's tactics because they taught it.
Orders come from the wing commander. Do what you are told.
The reward is paid whether or not the day is won, if you stay to the end.
success: The rebels broke at {system}. You flew with the wing that took their picket line, and {faction} pays {reward}. The uprising is not over, but it has lost its fleet.
